meaning:
ἀνα-σείω
[in Aq.: 1Ki.26:19, Job.2:3; Aq., Sm.: Isa.36:18 * ;]
1. to shake out, shake back, move to and fro (Thuc., a1.).
2. In late writers (Diod., al.; see MM, VGT, see word), to stir up; metaphorically, to excite: τ. ὄχλον, Mrk.15:11; τ. λαόν, Luk.23:5.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”
